newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico announces massive debt refinancing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico announces massive debt refinancing.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry on Tuesday announced a huge debt refinancing involving a decision to prepay $6 billion in floating-rate bank notes, including the issue of $1 billion of five-year floating rate bonds.

It also raised the amount of a 10-year global bond issued in January 1997 to $1.5 billion from $1 billion and said it would wrap up a $400 million bank credit and $1.1 billion medium-term note program shortly.
The refinancing would cut its average maturing debt for the next three years to $935 million per year, the Finance Ministry said.

It said the $6 billion prepayment would be made on Aug. 6, and would amortize bank notes issued on Aug. 5 last year to pay back the U.S. Treasury for an emergency bail-out during Mexico's 1994-5 peso crisis.
The resources to pay back the bank notes would come from the following sources, the Finance Ministry said:
1) Recent operations in international capital markets worth $2.5 billion
-- $590 million from a five-year Japanese Samurai bond (April 1997)
-- $200 million from a seven-year bank credit (May 1997)
-- $490 million from a five-year sterling bond (May 1997)
-- $930 million from "other operations" of the Federal Government in international capital markets, as well as from dollar earnings from government financial assets (Jan-June 1997)
2)Current operations in international capital markets worth $2 billion
-- $500 million as a result of increasing the amount of a 10-year global bond issued in Jan. 1997 to $1.5 billion from $1 billion
-- $1 billion from the issue of a five-year floating-rate note
-- Operations under a medium-term note program for $500 million
3) Operations to be completed in coming weeks worth $1.5 billion
-- Operations under a medium-term note program worth $1.1 billion, mostly to be issued in the European market
